items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...He never talked much about himself, but he had plenty to say about Umber Simeon, for example, and Freddie Kepler and Perez. Yeah, that's right. He liked them. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, he liked them.

ctx.x: I heard his name, but I think it was according to Saints. I don't remember. But there were players playing places that I would stand on the sidewalk and listen to me and never had an idea who was playing inside. Oh, boy. Jolly, Jolly was not like a lot of people imagine. As far as I was concerned, he didn't do much bragging with me. He would state what he thought, you know. Yeah, well, that's, I remember, as the not bragging. But he depended, I think, in my case, I think he depended on the fact that he knew I…

Well, I used to talk to him, and then, because I asked him about a lot of other musicians and all that, you know. He never talked much about himself, but he had plenty to say about Umber Simeon, for example, and Freddie Kepler and Perez. Yeah, that's right. He liked them.

Yeah, he liked them. And the funny thing about that, see, I had, I'd been pretty much out of Bud Rack time and enough. To about 1925, I'd bought a few records now and then, most with piano records. But in 1925, I started going to night school, and I was working daytime, and I didn't have time for anything else. So I dropped out of my life entirely, almost, to music. I didn't play much. My nephew came low, he was playing, and I wouldn't pay much attention. So, I started to tell something I'm going to forget. What…
